Residential Parking Permit
Frequently asked questions
The Residential Parking Permit (RPP) Program helps protect neighborhoods from documented,
recurring parking impacts caused by non-residential vehicles. It is designed to address
situations where outside parking demand substantially interferes with residents’ ability to
access on-street parking near their homes. RPP responds to demonstrated conditions, not
anticipated or hypothetical impacts.

5 Are visitor passes available? Yes.
Residents may purchase a two-week visitor pass for
$15.
Visitor passes are intended for short-term guests and
temporary needs. They are not designed for long-term
vehicle storage.
Short-term visitor passes are currently issued as paper
permits but being phased out. Many cities are
transitioning to digital guest passes, and the City is
evaluating future enhancements to improve
convenience and reduce misuse.
6 Are permits physical No.
stickers? All annual residential permits are issued electronically
and linked to the vehicle’s license plate number.
The only physical permit issued is the short-term, two-
week visitor pass, which is paper-based.
Enforcement is conducted using license plate
recognition technology and electronic verification.
7 What happens if parking If conditions materially change and documented
conditions change? evidence shows recurring non-residential interference,
residents may request a new study for evaluation.
8 How is eligibility determined? Eligibility is based on objective criteria established in
City Code, including:
On-street parking occupancy levels
Frequency and regularity of non-residential vehicles
Evidence of substantial interference
Property owner support
All required criteria must be met before a zone can be
established.
9 What if I am having a party? RPP is used where on-street parking is already limited—
it doesn’t create new spaces, it prioritizes existing ones.
That means capacity remains tight, and residents (and
their guests) must plan accordingly. For gatherings,
options include using visitor passes, encouraging
carpooling or rideshare, or directing guests to nearby
public or unrestricted parking.
